**Confirmation:** the assessments disagreed

First assessment `true`: structural: The structural obligations in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.StructuralQuery` are the `#[non_exhaustive]` struct and its public fields: `scope: SourceScope`, `language: LanguageId`, `rule: Map<String, Value>` and `limit: Option<usize>`. They also include the builder signatures `new(language, rule) -> Self`, `scope(self, scope) -> Self` and `limit(self, limit: usize) -> Self`. Together with the defaults, they are implemented by the supplied roots.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/public.rs#struct[StructuralQuery]` declares `#[non_exhaustive]` and exactly those four public fields with the stated types. A different field type, such as `Option<u32>` for `limit`, would change the prescribed type even if runtime results were the same.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/public.rs#impl[StructuralQuery]/fn[new]` has the prescribed signature. It sets `scope` to `SourceScope::all()`, which gives the "all visible files" default. It sets `limit` to `None`, which gives "no match limit". It stores `language` and `rule` as given.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/public.rs#impl[StructuralQuery]/fn[scope]` takes `self` by value, replaces `scope` and returns `Self`.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/public.rs#impl[StructuralQuery]/fn[limit]` takes `self` by value and a `usize`, sets `limit = Some(limit)` and returns `Self`.

The remaining clauses describe how a search behaves: `language` selects the grammar, `rule` is the ast-grep rule, and `limit` bounds matches across files. These are observable search behavior, not structural obligations on this type. I treated them as behavioral and left them to the behavioral criterion. I did not inspect `SourceScope::all()`, since the default it supplies is the observable behavior the text states.

behavioral: The tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.graph.search.StructuralQuery`. Both reviewed tests carry `{test}` references to it. I did not request implementation source.

The main test is `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[built_in_languages_and_structural_search_use_the_project_scope]`. It covers these obligations:

- **Defaults from `new(language, rule)`:**
  - It asserts `query.limit == None`.
  - A default-scope search finds only `visible.rs`. It does not return matches from `hidden.rs`, `skip/` or `.git`, which are ignored or hidden. That shows the default scope covers all visible files.
  - After `another.rs` is added, the same query returns both Rust files with `complete == true`. That shows the default limit is unbounded.
- **`scope` narrows the search:**
  - `SourceScope::under` with `hidden.rs`, `skip` or `.git` returns no matches.
  - `SourceScope::under("visible.rs")` returns the `visible.rs` match.
  - `SourceScope::under("..")` returns an error.
- **`limit` bounds matches across files:**
  - `limit(0)` gives 0 matches and `complete == false`.
  - `limit(1)` with one matching file gives 1 match and `complete == true`.
  - `limit(1)` with two matching Rust files gives exactly 1 match and `complete == false`. That is the cross-file bound.
- **`language` selects the grammar:**
  - The same rule with `"python"` returns only `script.py`. The Rust query does not return `script.py`.
  - `"plain-text"` fails with an unsupported-language error.
- **`rule` holds the ast-grep rule object:** the `{"rule":{"pattern":"call()"}}` map produces a match with excerpt `call()` and selector `fn[visible]`.

The struct and method signatures, including the public fields and the builder methods `scope` and `limit`, are exercised by compiling and using them in this test. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the exported inventory against rustdoc. It also checks that the shipping Habeas consumer compiles against the SDK. No observable behavioral obligation is left without a test.

Second assessment `false`: In `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[built_in_languages_and_structural_search_use_the_project_scope]`, add an assertion that `StructuralQuery::scope` narrows the results among several visible matching files. After `another.rs` is written, so that `visible.rs` and `another.rs` both match, search with `.scope(SourceScope::under("visible.rs"))` and assert that only `visible.rs` is returned. Also assert that `.scope(SourceScope::under("another.rs"))` returns only `another.rs`. — The requirement says `scope` narrows the search. The marked test only scopes queries to `hidden.rs`, `skip` and `.git`, which are ignored or hidden anyway, so they return nothing even if the scope is not applied. The `under("visible.rs")` query runs when `visible.rs` is the only visible match, so it returns the same result as an unscoped search. The `under("..")` assertion only shows that an invalid scope errors. A `scope()` that validated the scope but did not filter matches would pass every assertion. The one other scope check, in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/tests.rs#fn[structural_search_uses_overridden_parses_their_snapshot_and_requested_scope]`, only shows that the scope reaches the provider. It matches a single file, so it does not show narrowing. It also has no `{test}` reference to `requirements.sdk.graph.search.StructuralQuery`.

Recorded the second assessment (`false`).

text: `StructuralQuery::new(language, rule)` searches all visible files with no match

limit. `scope` and `limit` narrow the search. `language` selects the grammar, and `rule` holds the ast-grep rule object. `limit` bounds the number of matches across files. `None` leaves the count unbounded.
pub fn new(language: LanguageId, rule: Map<String, Value>) -> Self;
pub fn scope(self, scope: SourceScope) -> Self;
pub fn limit(self, limit: usize) -> Self;
